current.text: Dereck Lively, Dharma and Morez Johnson Jr. are hurt, which leaves Gafford as the likely opening night center.
Gafford barely played in Dallas's first preseason game, even with P.J. Washington and Lively out.
Experts disagree on his early-season value. One sees possible top 100 value for a month or two if he starts while the other centers are hurt. The newest note doubts he will do much.
Josh ranks him in the 130 to 160 range. He sees him as a late flyer while Lively is out, but not once Lively is healthy.
He is worth drafting only if he starts at center. Josh calls him and Morez Johnson Jr. interchangeable as Dallas's late swing and stash picks.
Dallas has shopped him, and three different front offices have tried to trade him.
Nick expects Gafford to be traded.
Dusty May is the new head coach. Nobody knows yet how he will split center minutes between Lively, Gafford, Powell, Johnson and forwards like Washington and Aldama.
Josh's projected Dallas starting five has Morez Johnson Jr. at center, not Gafford.
Dallas has a 4-4-4 schedule in our playoff weeks, probably the best in the league. It also has a league-high 16 back-to-backs.
Dallas has no pick of its own, so it has no reason to tank.

durable.text: He has had recurring ankle problems. They hurt his play last season.
His finishing at the rim and his block rate have dropped from elite levels.
His FG% is a league outlier and lifts a team's FG%. His blocks are well above the pool.
He is not a great points league play.

note: Both sites price him as a last-dollar pick (Yahoo 1 USD, rank 131; ESPN 2 USD, rank 115). That puts him right at the edge of our 144-player draft, so take him for 1 USD only as a bench flyer for FG% and blocks in punt 3PM or punt FT builds. Before tipoff, check whether he starts on opening night and how many minutes Dusty May gives him while Lively is out. If he barely plays, as he did in the first preseason game, or Dallas trades him, drop him for waiver centers.
